messages.subject: Função fieldPolygon
messages.body_plain:
Olá, Filipe.

Gostaria de saber, se com a função fieldPolygon, tendo as minhas imagens padronizadas, e querer selecionar sempre a mesma área, consigo definir as coordenadas para usar a função de Parallel? E deixar essa seleção automatizada.

EX.shapeFile<-fieldPolygon(EX1,extent = T)

Desde já, obrigado pela atenção.

messages.subject: Re: Função fieldPolygon
messages.body_plain:
Olá Raylson,

 A resposta e SIM, você pode usar o mesmo polígono como shape para extrair informação de várias imagens em paralelo. O mais importante e saber que as imagens devem compartilhar o mesmo GIS e representar o mesmo local.

 O código abaixo e apenas para quando deseja selecionar toda a área da imagem (extent = T):

 EX.shapeFile<-fieldPolygon(EX1,extent = T)

Se você pertente usar apenas parte da imagem deve colocar extent = F e selecionar o polígono que deseja. Mais informações: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P15

Espero que isso ajude.

 Abs,

Filipe

messages.subject: Re: FIELDimageR: Re: Imagem escurecendo
messages.body_plain:
Oi Igor,

Obrigado por responder as perguntas.

Eu ainda não consegui entender o porquê isso está acontecendo. O valor médio do plote vai mudar se você retirou ou não o solo; se o shapefile esta exatamente como a primeira vez; se reduziu drasticamente a resolução da imagem; entre outros. Não tem nenhum argumento dentro das funções para mudança de valores. Vou continuar investigando assim que tiver um tempinho e caso descubra algo eu te informarei. Por favor, caso descubra algo compartilhe aqui também.

Obrigado,

Filipe

messages.subject: Re: FIELDimageR: Re: Função fieldPolygon
messages.body_plain:
Olá, Filipe.

Tentei fazer aqui, mas não consegui.

Usei essa função, troquei o T por F para selecionar a parte da imagem, mas quando eu carrego uma imagem nova para usar a mesma região.
Retorna as informações da imagem anterior.

Como devo proceder?
 EX.shapeFile<-fieldPolygon(EX1,extent = T)

# SELECIONA UM INDICE PARA OS OBJETOS  E REMOVER O FUNDO
EX1.I1<- fieldIndex(mosaic = EX.shapeFile$cropField,index = c("SI","BGI","BI","VARI","GLI","SI","SCI"),myIndex=c("Red"))

# REMOVE O FUNDO
EX1.R1<- fieldMask(mosaic = EX.shapeFile$cropField@extent,
                   index = "BGI",
                   cropValue = 0.7,
                   cropAbove = T)

Estou usando dessa forma.

messages.subject: Re: Using Mask from QGIS
messages.body_plain:
Hi Erik,

The problem is because there are some NAs in your mask and your plants are represented by the value 1 (FIELDimageR default is 0, for intern analysis). You can fix this issue by changing NAs to the background values (in your case is 0) and pixels with values >0 to 1 (representing plants). Also, you should not forget to change the minValue to the minimum size of the object that you are trying to select. The default is 0.01 (in your case I changed it to 0.0005).

Here is the code:

# Packages

library(FIELDimageR)

library(raster)

library(rgdal)

# Loading image

i1 = stack("excessGreen_binary.tif")

i1<-aggregate(i1,fact=4) # Reducing the image resolution for fast analysis (optional)

plot(i1)

# Shapefile

i1.shape = fieldPolygon(mosaic = i1,extent = T) # Selects the whole picture area as shapefile

# Preparing the mask

i1[is.na <http://is.na>(i1)]<-0 # The function do not accept NA (NA must be changed to the background value. In your case is 0)

i1[i1>0]<-1 # Mask values must be 0 or 1 (If the value is >0 must be changed to 1)

hist(i1)

table(as.matrix(i1))

# Counting number of Plants

i1.SC<-fieldCount(mosaic = i1,

                  fieldShape = i1.shape$fieldShape,

                  value = 1, # Your plants are represented by value 1

                  minSize = 0.0005 # Normally the default is 0.01 (always check the i1.SC$objectReject to select the minimum object size value)

                  )

i1.SC$objectSel

i1.SC$objectReject

Hope it helps you..!!!

Thank you,
Filipe

messages.subject_clean: Regarding with Counting the number of Ear of wheat
messages.body_plain:
Hi
Sudhir,

Thanks for
asking. The pipeline is basically the same...!

You need to
segment the image with one index that allows better identification of the ears
and removing leaves and soil. After that, you can draw the shapefile to count
the number of identified ears per plot.

However, the
current method for doing image segmentation in FIELDimageR is called
thresholding. This method probably will not do a good job once that ear and
leaves have similar colors. For that you need to develop a index to identify
perfectly only the ears (it will required some investigation and time). Another
solution is to use machine learning algorithms from other software, but for
that is required training the models (annotate images).

As soon as I have
new features about counting ears I will post here and let you know.

Please, let us know if you find a good segmentation index or any other solution (e.g., which software/pipeline that you decided to use) ...!

All the best,

Filipe

On Mon, Apr 26, 2021 at 8:17 PM fmatias <filipem...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Sudhir,
>
>
>
> Thanks for asking. The pipeline is basically the same...!
>
>
>
> You need to segment the image with one index that allows better identification of the ears and removing leaves and soil. After that, you can draw the shapefile to count the number of identified ears per plot.
>
>
>
> However, the current method for doing image segmentation in FIELDimageR is called thresholding. This method probably will not do a good job once that ear and leaves have similar colors. For that you need to develop a index to identify perfectly only the ears (it will required some investigation and time). Another solution is to use machine learning algorithms from other software, but for that is required training the models (annotate images).
>
>
>
> As soon as I have new features about counting ears I will post here and let you know.
>
>
>
> Please, let us know if you find a good segmentation index or any other solution (e.g., which software/pipeline that you decided to use) ...!
>
>
>
> All the best,
>
> Filipe
>
>

> >
> >

> > I have attached the wheat ear orthomosaic for your reference.
> >
> >
> > Kindly suggest for the same.
> >
> >
> > Thank you,
> > Sudhir

I have to repeat my question because I didn't solve my problem with the image rotation with the function fieldRotate.
The problem is when I try to rotate the image (which is in tiff format) I have bad results, plots are unnaturally distorted and shortened, because of that, I can't border individual plots in a good way with the function fieldShape.
The images are attached.
The image is exported from the project created in the Agisoft program.
Does someone have a solution for this problem?

Best regards,

Pedja
